msa.title: Module Assessment: File Handling & Low-Level I/O

questions.question: What data type is returned by `fopen()` in C to represent an open file stream?
questions.explanation: fopen() returns a pointer to a FILE control structure (FILE *) defined in <stdio.h>, or NULL on failure.

questions.question: What mode string should be passed to `fopen` to append data to the end of an existing file without overwriting it?
questions.explanation: "a" opens a file in append mode. All write operations are placed at the end of the file.

questions.question: What does `fopen("data.txt", "w")` do if `data.txt` already exists on disk?
options: Truncates the existing file to zero length, erasing all previous contents
questions.explanation: "w" mode creates a new file or truncates an existing file to length 0, completely overwriting prior contents.

questions.question: Why is calling `fclose(fp)` mandatory when finished with a file in C?
options: To flush remaining write buffers to disk and release system file descriptors
To delete the file from the OS
To prevent the computer from shutting down
questions.explanation: fclose() flushes the stream buffer to disk and releases the operating system file descriptor, preventing file corruption and resource leaks.

questions.question: Which function is designed for reading raw binary blocks of data from a file stream?
questions.explanation: fread(&buffer, size, count, fp) reads count elements of size bytes directly from a binary stream.

questions.question: What does `fseek(fp, 0, SEEK_END);` accomplish?
options: Moves the file position indicator to the very end of the file
Rewinds to the beginning of the file
questions.explanation: fseek with SEEK_END sets the stream position indicator relative to the end of the file (0 offset moves to the exact end).

questions.question: How can you compute the total size in bytes of a file using standard C file functions?
questions.explanation: Seeking to SEEK_END and then querying ftell() returns the byte offset from the start of the file, giving the total file size.

questions.question: Why should you test `while (!feof(fp))` with caution when reading files in C?
options: feof only returns true AFTER an attempted read operation fails on EOF, risking processing the last item twice
feof works only on binary files
questions.explanation: feof() returns true only after a read function has already attempted to read past the end. Prefer checking the return value of the read function itself.

questions.question: What are the three predefined standard streams automatically opened for every C program?
questions.explanation: Every C program automatically has access to standard input (stdin), standard output (stdout), and standard error (stderr).

questions.question: What is the binary mode modifier appended to file mode strings on Windows systems (e.g. `"rb"`, `"wb"`)?
options: To prevent automatic conversion between CRLF (\r\n) and LF (\n)
To run code with admin privileges
questions.explanation: On Windows, text mode translates \n to \r\n; appending "b" (binary mode) disables translation, preserving raw byte sequences.
